captions.text: Search the theorem to review: press /.
There are two MainTheorems: take the one in Dim24.
Mark it as the target of the review.
The side panel lists the targets, with their progress.
Rests on · Uses: everything the theorem uses.
Zoom in: a view of just that, in a tab of its own.
The view is laid out for what it holds alone.
Drag a cluster with Ctrl held: it stays there, for everyone.
Or let the lock go with l, and drag without Ctrl.
Double-click a circle to fold it to a point; again to open.
Space opens the source of what is selected.
Rest on a name: Lean says what it is.
Click it to go there: its source, its panel.
Keys: the definitions that carry what it says.
Mark each as a key with the mouse, in its panel.
Rests on · Keys lights them, joined to the target.
Selection: the statement alone.
Least effort — you trust every name in it.
Keys: the few that carry the meaning.
Little effort, good confidence.
TCB: everything it rests on.
Most effort, most confidence.
Choose how far to read: the counts say what each costs.
Read a definition, then say what you think of it.
Approve it, with why: the comment stays with it.
The target's progress counts your approval.
The Project tab: the whole codebase.
Every board shows the same review.
Share → AI agent: a token, and a prompt for it.
Paste the prompt into your agent: it joins here.
The token is the agent's own: revoke it here.
Click the agent to follow it, and ask.
It reads the code, and takes your view along.
Its answer names what it explains.
Library: add a paper about the code.
Link it to the theorem, at its page.
Space: its source, and the paper beside it at its page.
Pin a note on the target: where to start.
Export prints a view: here, the target's TCB.
Drag a section to change the document's order.
Typeset: the PDF follows the order you set.
Artwork: the board as a picture to keep.
Frame it, then save it as PNG or SVG.
